implementation_notes: TypeScript's `sdk` clients (AWS SDK v3, GCP clients) ship hand-written types, which makes the seam unusually cheap: you can declare your own narrow interface with the two operations you need and let the SDK object satisfy it structurally, with no base class and no wrapper class. The lock-in that TypeScript cannot fix is in configuration — environment variable names that mirror one provider's keys — and in the strongly-typed config schema, which is part of your contract and must be provider-neutral if you want to swap. ESLint's `no-restricted-imports` per directory is the enforcement mechanism, since the compiler will not express 'vendor SDK only in adapters'.
idiom_name: provider SDK types in domain interfaces; provider config keys in env
pitfalls: Structural typing means the SDK object satisfies your interface by accident, which is convenient until the SDK adds a conflicting member.
Provider-specific environment variable names in `.env` couple the deployment environment to one cloud, not just the code.
A discriminated union of provider configs ('aws' | 'gcp' | 'azure') puts every provider's option type in your own types, which is a partial re-export of the lock.
